text:
Maya Chen: Heads up — I'm porting the Python batching+KV sample into the new Optimize SDK snippets. Running into a weird spike in cache misses when combining kv-prefetch with a 4-bit quant profile and batch_size > 8. Repro below, any ideas? :eyes:

Tomás Rivera: Can you paste the minimal repro and the quant profile you're using? Also which runtime (hosted/dedicated/private) and GPU type?

Maya Chen: Repro (condensed):

```python
from redwood import OptimizeClient
client = OptimizeClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_KEY}")

# naive batching + kv prefetch
requests = [ {"input": "short question {}".format(i)} for i in range(32) ]
resp = client.generate_batch(
    model="open-4bit-v1",
    inputs=requests,
    batch_size=12,
    use_kv_prefetch=True,
    quant_profile="4bit-fast"
)
print(resp.metrics.cache_hits, resp.metrics.cache_misses)
```

Logs show cache_misses jumping ~3x when batch_size >= 12. On smaller batches (<=8) it's fine. Running on Dedicated (A10G pool) with runtime v2.1.

Liam O'Neill: Hm. Two quick thoughts: 1) If prefetch requests are issued per-shard or per-worker we can oversubscribe the KV cache lifecycle, causing evictions that look like misses. 2) 4-bit kernels sometimes change tokenization alignment in our prefetched-prefix heuristics.

Sophie Patel: Could be both. We hit a related edge last quarter where continuous batching + kv-prefetch race caused early evicts under heavy micro-batching. Workaround then was to set `kv_prefetch_batch_size` smaller than `batch_size`, e.g. 4 when batch_size is 12, so prefetches don't bump out active entries. Worth testing.

Maya Chen: Trying that now. Quick test: set `kv_prefetch_batch_size=4` -> cache_misses down by ~60%. Patch seems trivial but we should document the caveat and show the recommended values in the Optimize playbook/snippet.

Tomás Rivera: If that's reproducible, let's do two things: 1) update the Python snippet to include a small note and example config, 2) add a short JS snippet showing the same safety guard so customers using the SDKs don't trip. Also add a TOC entry under "Batching & KV prefetch".

Maya Chen: Draft for the docs note (short):

"When using kv-prefetch with aggressive batching and low-precision quant profiles, we recommend tuning 'kv_prefetch_batch_size' separately from 'batch_size'. Large prefetch batches can evict active cache entries on some runtimes, increasing miss rates. As a safe default set kv_prefetch_batch_size = min(4, batch_size)."

Sophie Patel: +1. Could also add an instrument snippet to the dashboard guidance: show cache_hits/misses per-route so teams can spot regressions. I can add the dashboard query.

Liam O'Neill: For the snippet itself, here's a tiny JS addition that mirrors the python guard:

```js
// ensure prefetch batch smaller than main batch to avoid evictions
const batchSize = 12;
const kvPrefetchBatch = Math.min(4, batchSize);
client.generateBatch({ model: 'open-4bit-v1', inputs, batchSize, kvPrefetchBatch, quantProfile: '4bit-fast' })
```

Maya Chen: Nice. I'll push a small docs PR with both snippets + the note. Creating branch now.

docs-bot: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1427 "optimize: batch/kv prefetch caveat + cross-sdk examples" — assigned to @MayaChen, reviewers @sophie @tomasr.

Tomás Rivera: I'll review. Can we also add a short test in the docs examples CI that runs the tiny repro (mocked runtime) to assert cache_misses doesn't increase above X? Prevents regressions.

Maya Chen: Good call — I can add a smoke test in examples/ci that runs with mocked metrics and validates <20% miss rate for the reference config.

Sophie Patel: I'll add the dashboard query and a screenshot to the PR.

Liam O'Neill: One more thing — add an item to the Optimize migration checklist about "validate kv-prefetch behavior when switching quant profiles". We saw customers change quantization and accidentally toggle caching behavior.

Maya Chen: Added to PR description checklist. Will merge once reviews/CI green. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Tomás Rivera: Thanks — great catch and good cross-sdk coverage.

Maya Chen: (after merge) merged — follow-up card created: MKT-2389 to surface this caveat in release notes and the Optimize quickstart.
